    Theorem A: Characterizations of E-finite algebras #

    This file assembles the three parts of Theorem A (intro:main) in the right-module convention (Rᵐᵒᵖ) of the manuscript:

    • equivalences_arbitraryField (Theorem A(I)): over an arbitrary field k, E-finiteness (E-fin) is equivalent to each of the seventeen module-theoretic, categorical, numerical, homological, and ring-theoretic conditions (K₀-Hom), (mon-dim), (comp-tors), (num-disj), (wide), (wide₁), (brick-label), (n-sbrick), (fin-sbrick), (brick-discrete), (endo-stab), (poly-brick), (no-gen-brick), (no-gen-grain), (thick-gen), (univ-loc), and (ring-epi).
    • equivalences_infiniteField (Theorem A(II)): when k is infinite, E-finiteness is also equivalent to (dim-brick) (Schur-representation-finiteness) and (dim-stab).
    • equivalences_algebraicallyClosedField (Theorem A(III), Theorem 6.1): when k is algebraically closed, E-finiteness is also equivalent to (moduli-pt), (open-brick), and (open-wide).
    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.equivalences_arbitraryField (k R : Type u) [Field k] [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] :
    (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ EqualClassHom (FGModuleCat Rᵐᵒᵖ)) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ∀ (T : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty (FGModuleCat Rᵐᵒᵖ)), T.IsClosedUnderQuotients → T.IsClosedUnderExtensions → T 0 → Function.Injective ⇑(GrothendieckMonoid.dimensionMap T)) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ∀ (M : FGModuleCat Rᵐᵒᵖ), FunctoriallyFinite (generatedTorsionClass M)) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ NumericallyDisjointTorsionPairs (FGModuleCat Rᵐᵒᵖ)) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ∀ (W : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty (FGModuleCat Rᵐᵒᵖ)), IsWideClass W → FunctoriallyFinite W) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ∀ (B : FGModuleCat Rᵐᵒᵖ), IsBrick B → FunctoriallyFinite (FilteredBy B)) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ BrickLabels Rᵐᵒᵖ) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ∀ (s : Set (CategoryTheory.Skeleton (FGModuleCat Rᵐᵒᵖ))), IsSemibrick s → s.Finite → s.ncard = (simpleIsomorphismClasses Rᵐᵒᵖ).ncard → s = simpleIsomorphismClasses Rᵐᵒᵖ) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ∀ (s : Set (CategoryTheory.Skeleton (FGModuleCat Rᵐᵒᵖ))), IsSemibrick s → s.Finite) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ∀ (r : ℕ), 0 < r → (brickClassesOfEndolength k r).Finite) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ∀ (g : ProjectiveClass Rᵐᵒᵖ) (r : ℕ), 0 < r → (stableClassesOfEndolength k ((projectiveClassWeight k) g) r).Finite) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ PolynomialBrickGrowth Rᵐᵒᵖ) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ¬∃ (M : ModuleCat Rᵐᵒᵖ), IsGenericBrick k M) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ¬∃ (M : ModuleCat Rᵐᵒᵖ), IsGenericGrain k M) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ∀ (H : TwoTerm Rᵐᵒᵖ → Prop), TwoTerm.IsBoundedTwoTermThick H → ∃ (U : TwoTerm Rᵐᵒᵖ), U.IsPresilting ∧ ∀ (X : TwoTerm Rᵐᵒᵖ), H X ↔ (CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.singleton U.inBoundedProjectives).triangEnvelope X.inBoundedProjectives) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ RightUniversalLocalizationsFinite k R) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ∀ (B : Type u) [inst : Ring B] [IsSimpleRing B] [IsArtinianRing B] (f : R →+* B) (hf : IsRingEpimorphism f), Module.Finite k B)

    Theorem A(I): Over an arbitrary field, E-finiteness (E-fin) is equivalent to each of the seventeen conditions (K₀-Hom) through (ring-epi), listed in manuscript order.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.equivalences_infiniteField (k R : Type u) [Field k] [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [Infinite k] :
    (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ∀ (d : ↑(simpleIsomorphismClasses Rᵐᵒᵖ) → ℕ), (brickClassesOfClass (classOfCompositionVector k d)).Finite) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ ∀ (g : ProjectiveClass Rᵐᵒᵖ) (d : ↑(simpleIsomorphismClasses Rᵐᵒᵖ) → ℕ), (stableClassesOfClass ((projectiveClassWeight k) g) (classOfCompositionVector k d)).Finite)

    Theorem A(II) (Corollary 5.4): Over an infinite field, E-finiteness is also equivalent to finiteness of bricks of each dimension vector (dim-brick) and finiteness of θ-stable bricks of each dimension vector (dim-stab).

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.equivalences_algebraicallyClosedField (k R : Type u) [Field k] [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsAlgClosed k] :
    (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ (basicPresentation k R).KingClosedPointCondition) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ (basicPresentation k R).OpenBrickOrbits) ∧ (IsEFinite Rᵐᵒᵖ ↔ (basicPresentation k R).OpenWideLoci)

    Theorem A(III) (Theorem 6.1): Over an algebraically closed field, E-finiteness is also equivalent to (moduli-pt) (at most one closed point in each King moduli space), (open-brick) (every brick has an open orbit), and (open-wide) (every wide locus is open).
